papers.title: A Computational and Experimental Framework for Fourier Optics in Python
papers.abstract: Simulation of the propagation of light is useful for the design and dimensioning of optical systems. In this paper, we present the basics of propagation simulation using Fourier optics and practical implementation in Python, with a particular emphasis on dimensions. We first verify that our numerical wave-optics simulations maintain correct physical spatial scaling. Next, we benchmark numerical propagation against closed-form analytical formulas for Gaussian beams, lens focusing effects, and grating diffraction. We then show how those simulations can be used to generate diffractive optical elements such as Fresnel zone plates, and we bridge the gap between numerical simulations and experiments by collecting data and recovering phase information using a phase retrieval algorithm.

papers.title: Nodal Knotted Finite-Energy Spatiotemporally Localized Scalar Wave Solutions
papers.abstract: Significant amount of information is available in wave optics about monochromatic paraxial beams characterized by nodal knots, the latter being threads of complete darkness (lines of zero intensity) tied into knots. Also, well -known are finite-energy spatiotemporally localized vector-valued wave solutions characterized by knotted to-pologies. Unfortunately, except for solutions to the Schr\"odinger-like equation describing anomalous dispersion, no scalar-valued spatiotemporally localized waves with analogous knotted topological structures are known to date. It is the goal in this article to fill in this gap by deriving finite-energy spatiotemporally localized scalar-valued wave solutions characterized specifically by Hopf and trefoil nodal knot topologies. This will extend to spatiotemporally localized pulsed fields the diverse important applications of mono-chromatic light beams, having nontrivial topological structures, in trapping and guiding particles, image processing and optical communications; also, in applications to biology and medicine.

papers.title: A universal modal-noise limit for multimode photonic systems
papers.abstract: Modal noise limits the photometric and spectroscopic stability of every multimode-to-single-mode photonic system, yet it is quantified device by device. For isotropic modal excitation at fixed input power, the fractional power fluctuation of any linear multimode system is shown to be fixed by one number: the participation ratio M_eff of the eigenvalues of K = T{\dag}WT. Monte Carlo for spatially filtered fibres, lossy lanterns, and integrated mode converters confirms the law, which recovers the classical speckle limits. Extending K to K({\lambda}) gives the spectral correlation of modal noise and a closed-form velocity error, maximal when the correlation width equals the line width.

papers.title: The Complete Set of Solutions for the Equations of Temporal Coupled Mode Theory
papers.abstract: Temporal coupled mode theory (TCMT) provides a compact description of resonant transport in optical systems in terms of a small set of physically transparent parameters, including the resonant coupling coefficients and direct background scattering matrix. In the formalism of TCMT, the background scattering matrix and the coupling vectors are constrained by time reversal symmetry, reciprocity, and energy conservation. While these constraints are well established, the general so- lution under these is only known for a few cases, in which spatial symmetry simplifies the problem. In this paper, we derive the complete set of solutions for the equations of temporal coupled mode theory that describes lossless single-mode or multi-mode resonators coupled to an arbitrary num- ber of ports. Our derivation utilizes an explicit Takagi decomposition of the symmetric unitary background scattering matrix. We provide a comparison with numerical simulations for both the single and multimode cases.

papers.title: High-Dimensional Structured Light Tomography with a Tilted Lens
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate high-dimensional spatial mode tomography using intensity measurements and the astigmatic transformation implemented with a tilted lens. We improve the method previously published in Ref. [1] to perform the spatial tomography not restricted to a fixed order, which allowed us to achieve good fidelity for a mode space dimension as high as $D=66\,$. Since the literature is not unanimous, we also present a comprehensive revision of light propagation through a tilted lens for an accurate description of the transformation used for tomography. We derive its effective focal lengths, and analyze its role as an astigmatic mode converter. Moreover, we establish its explicit domain of validity within the Hermite-Gaussian basis.

papers.title: A fast and accurate model for gradient-based inverse design of multimode waveguides
papers.abstract: Multimode photonic inverse design requires fast, accurate computational models that provide geometry gradients. Based on coupled-mode theory (CMT), we propose a differentiable surrogate model. Its parameter-extraction method uses a change of modal basis to obtain coupled-mode parameters from cross-sectional mode data. We also provide a complete, easy-to-implement propagation and optimization workflow. Using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulation data as a common reference, we compare the prediction accuracy of our model and forward dataset-based eigenmode expansion (EME) for randomly generated thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) waveguide profiles that traverse modal coupling regions. Using identical modal libraries, the model reduces the maximum per-mode mean absolute transmission error by 17-37% compared with forward EME. We demonstrate a spot-size converter design that preserves the fundamental TM$_0$ mode in its hybridization region with the first-order TE$_1$ mode and obtain nine structures, each with FDTD-verified transmission above 98%. These tests demonstrate the model's utility for large-scale photonic inverse design, enabling rapid exploration of the design parameter space by combining gradient information with improved prediction accuracy.

papers.title: High-fidelity six-dimensional optical data storage
papers.abstract: Multi-dimensional optical data storage, wherein each voxel encodes multiple bits of information within a three-dimensional isotropic medium, presents a revolutionary approach to dense data storage. This approach exploits multiple degrees of freedom of light, such as intensity, polarization and wavelength, to selectively control distinct optical responses in the medium. However, increasing dimensionality exacerbates crosstalk between different encoding dimensions, thereby compromising recording fidelity. In this study, we introduce a novel six-dimensional (6D) multiplexing approach that exploits ultrafast interactions of polarized light with a three-dimensional medium. By manipulating three light parameters within a Poincar\'e-like semi-sphere, we systematically induce three distinct material responses in laser-induced nanostructures, each corresponding to a unique physical quantity: fluorescence, phase retardance, and slow axis orientation. Thanks to such multiple one-to-one correspondence between light parameters and material responses, we achieve unprecedented high fidelity, attaining a raw accuracy of 99.45%. Furthermore, this independently controlled 6D multiplexing technique maximizes the effective user capacity to 0.38 petabits per disc. The versatility of laser-induced nanostructures across multiple physical dimensions enables diverse applications, ranging from high-capacity data storage to microfluidics, optical elements, integrated photonics, micromechanics, and quantum technologies.

papers.title: Direct measurement of the on-shot focal-spot size of a kilojoule-class petawatt laser
papers.abstract: We report a direct, on-shot determination of the focal-spot size of a kilojoule-class, four-beam petawatt laser. Encircled-energy curves were inferred from the energy transmitted around aluminum-coated spheres of varying diameters placed at the focal plane. The 50% encircled-energy diameter D50 of each beam was obtained by fitting a two-component Gaussian mixture with Bayesian inference. With all deformable mirrors optimized in closed loop, the best-corrected alignment beam reached D50 = 34 (+4/-5) um, three times the diffraction limit of 10 um. Under full-power conditions, the thermal distortion of the main amplifier broadened this beam to D50 = 102 (+9/-8) um and reduced its peak intensity ninefold, to 2.2 (+0.6/-0.9) x 10^18 W/cm^2 at 250 J and 1.3 ps. The energy fraction of the narrow component decreased from 68% to 38%. These reference values serve facility users, and a deformable mirror upstream of the pulse compressor, now on one beam only, doubles the on-shot peak intensity.

papers.title: Seamless Gradient Pixels for Multidimensional Optical Information Interrogation
papers.abstract: Information from light interaction with its environment can be extracted from its numerous properties. Yet capturing and interpreting this information within a single and compact platform remains challenging because conventional systems rely on discrete components and detection channels. Here we introduce the concept of "gradient pixels" that provides a universal metasurface platform to interrogate optical field information in the infrared (IR) spectrum. By continuously varying a design parameter across two dimensions, we encode multidimensional optical information into measurable spatial patterns, e.g., both spectral and polarization information are acquired from a single snapshot image. A free-form gradient pixel further enables prescribed wavelength-selective spatial patterns within a single metasurface through tailored gradient profiles. Unlike isolated filter arrays, seamless gradient-pixels multiplex neighbouring meta-atoms, increasing channel spatial density and relaxing Q-factor constraints. A 250-$\mu$m footprint of these meta-atoms achieves spectral resolution better than 100-pm over a 100-nm spectral span based on a serpentine configuration. Snapshot wavelength-polarization reconstruction yields polarization angular accuracy at 0.3$^\circ$. We extend this concept to perform near-field refractive index sensing at video rates using the same explicit parameter-space mapping. By linking far-field detection and near-field sensing, it enables spatially resolved analysis of optical fields and local dielectric environments through a common image-based readout. It offers prospects for multidimensional optical sensing, computational imaging and intelligent information processing.

papers.title: Real-Time Single-Pixel Imaging via Exploiting Temporal Mixing: A Unified Calibration and Composite Readout Framework
papers.abstract: In high-speed optical measurements and computational imaging such as in single-pixel imaging temporal mixing arising from the mismatch between modulation and the electro-optical acquisition chain is conventionally treated as an unmitigated distortion that corrupts measurement orthogonality, breaks compressive sensing priors, fundamentally limits imaging speed, and induces catastrophic reconstruction failure. Here, we establish a transferable, unified calibration and composite-readout framework for single-pixel imaging that systematically repurposes temporal memory from a readout limitation into a powerful measurement resource. Beyond achieving robust high-fidelity recovery, this engineered approach enables cost effective, lower bandwidth configurations to consistently deliver superior image quality compared to higher bandwidth reference setups across diverse operating conditions turning a historical hardware bottleneck into an active imaging advantage. Specifically, target scenes are reconstructed directly from mixed observations without the need to recover individual pattern projections, thereby significantly advancing high-speed and video-rate single-pixel imaging capabilities. Crucially, the transferability of our framework allows calibration routines established on one hardware platform (such as digital micromirror device-based setups) to be readily transferred across different optical systems (such as rotating coding disks), paving the way for calibrated temporal memory as a versatile and generalized measurement paradigm for broader computational imaging.

papers.title: Probing thin films and their interfaces via angle-resolved second-harmonic generation
papers.abstract: Increasing demands on the performance and reliability of optical thin films stimulate the development of more sensitive characterisation methods capable of investigating thin-film interfaces or local mechanical stress. Second-harmonic generation (SHG) is a phenomenon that can serve as a non-destructive probe, tracing local symmetry changes in the film surface, bulk, and buried interfaces. Here, we investigate the decomposition of the SHG response from these three regions by combining angle- and polarisation-resolved measurements. We utilised a theoretical model of SHG accounting for multiple reflections and optical interference in a thin layer. The theory was first experimentally evaluated using Ta2O5 films deposited on different glass substrates. The fitting procedure accurately reproduced the measured SHG responses, revealing pronounced substrate-dependent variations in the buried-interface contribution, while the surface and effective-bulk responses remained similar. As the next step, we studied the reliability of the SHG signal decomposition into the surface, bulk and buried-interface components. The decomposition was evaluated by generating synthetic datasets and testing whether their retrieval was unique and accurate. The influence of film thickness, measurement noise, uncertainties in linear-optical parameters, and the polarisation channels used on the retrieval of nonlinear susceptibilities was also examined. Our results demonstrate that reliable separation of SHG contributions requires accurate linear optical parameters, global fitting of multiple polarisation channels, and sufficiently pronounced interference features, outlining the capabilities and practical limitations of SHG-based region-specific characterisation of optical thin films.

papers.title: Sign-Controlled BIC Merging and Flatband Formation in C2-symmetric Photonic Lattices
papers.abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) on flatbands promise long-lived, weakly dispersive photons, yet their interplay remains elusive. Here, we develop a four-mode non-Hermitian Hamiltonian for $C_2$-symmetric photonic-crystal slabs. We show that the sign of the interpair coupling determines whether two Friedrich-Wintgen (FW) BICs and a symmetry-protected (SP) BIC occupy the same photonic band, a necessary condition for merging. In rectangular lattices, merging eliminates the quadratic radiative-loss term in a perfect-square form and strongly suppresses the quartic contribution, giving an effective $Q \sim k^{-6}$ scaling. Deviations from rectangular geometry induce noncollinear radiation polarizations, converting FW-BICs into quasi-BICs with $Q_{\mathrm{qBIC}} \sim (90^\circ-\theta)^{-2}$ and restoring the asymptotic $Q \sim k^{-2}$ scaling. Unlike BIC band selection, quadratic band flattening is insensitive to the coupling sign and can occur without BIC merging, even in oblique lattices. Our results reveal distinct conditions governing BIC merging, higher-order radiation suppression, and band flattening.

papers.title: Photonic processors that carry their own unclonable fingerprint
papers.abstract: Physically unclonable functions (PUFs) derive cryptographic keys from uncontrollable fabrication disorder, removing the need to store secrets in vulnerable non-volatile memory. Programmable photonic processors are natural candidates for PUFs, because each of their many tunable interferometers carries its own fabrication imperfections. However, we show that the mesh topology itself funnels light along short paths, so that most of this disorder contributes little to the response. Here we introduce an isotropic ring routing scheme that steers light to the core of a hexagonal mesh and redistributes it uniformly towards the perimeter, suppressing a distance-dependent power decay of 14.7 dB and raising the mean Shannon entropy of the response from 1.95 to 3.48 bits by reprogramming alone. Experiments on two independently fabricated 72-unit silicon processors show that a nominally identical device cannot reproduce the target's responses even after its passive phase profile is fully compensated. Combining isotropic routing with spectral readout yields 1107 bits per challenge, exceeding previous results by two orders of magnitude, with 49.8% inter-challenge and 50.0% inter-chip Hamming distances and a 4.9% intra-chip distance. These results establish general-purpose programmable photonic processors as reconfigurable, high-capacity hardware roots of trust.

papers.title: High-Speed Widefield Hyperspectral Imaging
papers.abstract: Fourier-transform hyperspectral imaging is an emerging technology that combines widefield acquisition with flexible spectral resolution. Yet, it typically requires the acquisition of dense sequences of full-field interferograms during optical-path scanning, which ultimately reduces the final throughput. To circumvent this limitation, this manuscript introduces an event-based Fourier-transform hyperspectral microscopy technique that exploits the coupling of a neuromorphic event camera with a common-path birefringent interferometer operated under continuous scanning. Specifically, two complementary acquisition strategies are investigated, one with steady broadband illumination where the event stream corresponds to a derivative-like interferogram, and another with a temporal modulation of a broadband LED, which produces an intensity-like event response. Both approaches are able to retrieve the principal spectral profiles of photographic filters, showing a good qualitative match with both frame-based and spectrometer references. Compared against the typical 15-minute acquisition time for step-scan reference configuration, both methods represent a speedup larger than 3 orders of magnitude, entering real-time acquisition speeds: the derivative-based method acquires the useful interferometric range in approximately 200 ms, corresponding to an effective rate of approximately 5 hyperspectral cubes per second, whereas the modulation-assisted method achieves an experimentally measured spectral resolution of 17.9 nm at an effective acquisition rate of 2.5 datacubes per second. Finally, reflection-mode imaging and motion-compensated reconstruction of moving particles further demonstrate spatially resolved spectral recovery beyond static transmission measurements, establishing the solution as a promising technology for continuous, wide-field hyperspectral imaging.

papers.title: DUV (257 nm) LIDT of Anti-Reflective Coatings
papers.abstract: Laser-induced damage threshold in the deep ultraviolet (DUV) was used to perform tests on AR coated windows intended for industrial processes. The 257 nm wavelength was generated from Yb:YAG fundamental (1030 nm) and the long-term LIDT stability (up to 100000 shots) was selected as representative for minimal industrial qualification. Selected setup for the fourth harmonics generation consists of two stages, generation of second harmonic and subsequently the fourth harmonic with 13,4% conversation efficiency. In both 1-on-1 and S-on-1 experiments, the optics coated with Al2O3/SiO2 by ion beam sputtering technique demonstrated the highest LIDT value of 0.73 and 0.5 J/cm2 respectively. Various damage morphologies, color centers, ballistic damage, delamination, and blistering were observed across the samples with respect to the 1-on-1 and S-on-1.

papers.title: Hybrid Plasmon-Phonon Eigenmodes and Vortex States in a Graphene Ring on a Silica Substrate
papers.abstract: We investigate hybrid plasmon-phonon eigenmodes and localized electromagnetic vortex states in a graphene ring supported by a dispersive silica substrate. The interaction between graphene plasmons and infrared-active optical phonons of the substrate gives rise to distinct spectral branches of surface polaritons, whose dispersion characteristics are established analytically and validated by full-wave numerical simulations. Geometric confinement of these hybrid surface excitations produces spectrally separated families of localized multipolar eigenmodes with corresponding azimuthal symmetries. Particular attention is devoted to quadrupolar eigenstates, which exhibit nearly identical normalized spatial field distributions despite their substantial spectral separation and different attenuation characteristics. We demonstrate that coherent superposition of orthogonal quadrupolar field patterns gives rise to localized vortex states with opposite azimuthal phase winding. The preservation of the spatial eigenmode structure across distinct spectral branches is consistent with a quasistatic description in which the resonator geometry governs the modal symmetry, whereas the dispersive material response determines the spectral properties. These findings reveal a route toward controlling structured electromagnetic near fields through plasmon--phonon hybridization and establish a physical basis for multiband vortex states in deeply subwavelength graphene resonators.

papers.title: High-Power Short-Wavelength Frequency Comb from Coherent Radiation of Uncompressed Electron Beams
papers.abstract: High-power frequency combs at short wavelengths would open new opportunities for precision measurements and high-resolution spectroscopy. Here, we propose a frequency comb based on coherent undulator radiation from uncompressed electron bunches. An optical frequency comb serves as the seed, establishing a common phase reference for microbunching in successive electron bunches and transferring its phase coherence to short-wavelength harmonic radiation. By exploiting interference between distinct laser-induced microbunching pathways, we reduce the sensitivity of the harmonic bunching phase to electron-beam energy fluctuations, a major challenge for maintaining interpulse coherence. Start-to-end simulations demonstrate frequency comb generation in the vacuum-ultraviolet (148 nm) and soft X-ray regimes, yielding average radiation powers of approximately 1 W and 100 mW, respectively, with approximately 6 $\mu$W and 100 nW concentrated in individual comb teeth. These results establish a promising route toward high-power, phase-coherent short-wavelength frequency combs for precision spectroscopy, including searches for the nuclear transition in trapped $^{229}$Th ions.

papers.title: A photon-number-conserving multimode framework for pulse propagation dynamics across zero nonlinearity: Kerr-Raman cooperation and competition
papers.abstract: Raman scattering in multimode fibers shifts pulse spectra to lower frequencies and transfers photons between spatial modes. When the nonlinear coefficient changes sign within the pulse spectrum, the ordinary generalized nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (GNLSE) can give unphysical predictions. Existing photon-number-conserving formulations either treat a single mode or exclude Raman scattering. We develop a time-domain multimode GNLSE that conserves photon number, includes the full Raman response and remains well defined at the zero-nonlinearity frequency. For narrowband pulses with a constant positive nonlinear coefficient, the framework reduces to the standard multimode GNLSE with instantaneous Kerr and delayed Raman terms. We then apply the framework to three coherently excited modes whose spectra shift across the zero-nonlinearity frequency. The Kerr and Raman processes first cooperate and then compete. In the first stage, both processes transfer photons into the fundamental mode, contributing about 2\% and 43\% of the initial total photon number. In the second stage, Kerr transfer drives photons out of the fundamental mode, while Raman transfer drives photons back, contributing about $-27\%$ and $+15\%$, respectively. Consequently, the fundamental-mode photon fraction rises from 20\% to 65\% and then falls to 53\%. Kerr terms that leave the modal photon populations unchanged still reshape the fields and thereby enhance Raman transfer. Moreover, changing only the relative input phases can reverse the initial Raman-driven flow into the fundamental mode, even for identical modal spectra. Taken together, the results show how instantaneous and delayed nonlinear responses, together with intermodal phase, govern photon redistribution across zero nonlinearity.

papers.title: Simulation-pretrained autoencoders versus PCA for compressing multimode fibre transmission matrices
papers.abstract: Multimode optical fibres can image through a thin, flexible probe once their transmission matrix (TM) has been measured, but a TM is large and must be re-measured whenever the fibre moves. A compact model of feasible TMs would make storing and re-estimating them cheaper, so we ask how compactly TMs can be represented, and from how few measured TMs. Here we benchmark a permutation-equivariant autoencoder, pretrained on simulated fibres and adapted to measured TMs, against principal component analysis (PCA). At 62x compression, adapting the pretrained autoencoder with just two measured TMs reconstructs the TM of a 50um fibre well enough to focus light at 98% of the ideal enhancement, and it stays accurate when the TMs are shifted by 25 pixels or zoomed by 10%, which quickly degrades a linear basis. It is not, however, a better compressor: PCA is about ten times more accurate when fitted on all 163 real TMs (1.1% against 11.9% error on held-out TMs) and is already more accurate from ten. The autoencoder's value is as a prior when few or no real TMs exist: with none it reaches 29% error, against 91% for PCA fitted on the same simulation. Transfer to a different fibre is only partial. The most important extension, not yet tested, is to recover pixel-basis TMs from fewer measurements than a full TM, which would turn the pretrained prior from a compressor into a measurement-saving tool.

papers.title: Full Kummer Beams: Skyrmionic textures in bichromatic light
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce full Kummer beams, the bichromatic analog of full Poincar\'e beams. To this end, we define three parameters that characterize bichromatic states of polarization and span the Kummer shape, the bichromatic counterpart of the Poincar\'e sphere. We find that, under certain conditions, full Kummer beams can exhibit skyrmionic textures with a Skyrme number that depends not only on the topological charges but also on the frequencies. These beams can also exhibit emergent behavior upon propagation, including robust, higher-order-like structures and a propagation-invariant Skyrme number over a wide range of beam-waist selections.

papers.title: From power to spectrum: an off-the-shelf photodiode turned into a spectrometer by its bias alone
papers.abstract: Computational spectrometers replace dispersive optics with detectors whose spectral response can be varied, but every reported single-detector device obtains this response through dedicated fabrication: two-dimensional heterostructures, graded epitaxial junctions, organic stacks, filters or photonic circuits. We demonstrate a generic, fabrication-free alternative in which a standard commercial photodiode becomes a spectrometer through its electrical drive alone, requiring no modification of the device, no optical filter and no modulation of the light. The mechanism is bias-modulated optoelectronic chromatic dispersion (OED): light of different wavelengths is absorbed at different depths, and a sinusoidal bias changes how carriers generated at each depth are collected, so that every spectrum is encoded in the shape of the photocurrent waveform over one bias period. Applied to an unmodified InGaAs PIN photodiode at room temperature, a 10 us waveform decoded by a neural network reconstructs spectra of one to three laser lines across the 80 nm of the telecom C+L band, locating the lines to 0.3-0.4 nm, counting them in about 99% of measurements and identifying their power levels, with line shifts tracked to tens of picometres. Because OED relies on universal semiconductor transport physics, the approach is material-agnostic and applies in principle to any off-the-shelf photodiode, turning detectors already deployed as power monitors into low-cost spectral sensors.

papers.title: Distributed Fiber Monitoring on a Coherent DSP ASIC: Implementation of Longitudinal Power Monitoring
papers.abstract: Coherent DSP ASICs and transceivers to date report a rich set of optical link metrics, yet these remain cumulative over the link and provide no spatial localization. This paper presents the implementation design of fiber-longitudinal power monitoring (LPM), which recovers spatially resolved power profiles from received traffic, on a coherent DSP ASIC chip. We first identify the challenges specific to DSP implementation, and describe the enabling algorithm and architecture. We then present the key design considerations for retaining the estimation fidelity of the on-chip LPM during in-service operation. On this basis, we implement LPM on a coherent DSP, a 3-nm 800G low-power DSP ASIC housed in an OSFP pluggable module, which constitutes, to our knowledge, the first coherent DSP ASIC and transceiver to perform distributed fiber monitoring and data communication simultaneously. The on-chip LPM is experimentally validated over links of up to 1005 km using 400ZR+ and 800ZR+ traffic, with no measurable impact on Q factor or module power consumption. Multi-vendor interoperability is also demonstrated, where the on-chip LPM operates on signals transmitted by third-party transceivers. These results extend coherent DSPs from cumulative to spatially resolved monitoring, allowing pluggable transceivers, deployable from DCI to long-haul, to act not only as cost-efficient transmission elements but also as distributed monitoring points across diverse optical network infrastructure.

papers.title: Interfacing Silicon Nitride Nanophotonics with Cuprous Oxide Rydberg Excitons
papers.abstract: Rydberg excitons in cuprous oxide (Cu$_2$O), the solid-state counterpart of Rydberg atoms, are hydrogen-like electron--hole quasi-particles with micron-sized wavefunctions and strong long-range interactions that promise optical nonlinearities at the few-photon level. Exploiting them in a waveguide quantum electrodynamics (WQED) setting can enable what atomic Rydberg platforms achieve only with ultrahigh vacuum and laser cooling/trapping---a guided optical mode interfaced with the Rydberg medium---while adding the scalability and advanced fabrication of integrated photonics. Here we demonstrate a monolithic, CMOS-compatible interface of Cu$_2$O Rydberg excitons with a SiN$_x$ nanophotonic waveguide. Under non-resonant excitation, excitonic emission from the Cu$_2$O microcrystal is coupled to the guided mode, routed along the waveguide, and collected from an output grating. The spectrum shows the phonon-assisted 1$s$ orthoexciton emission together with the low-lying 2$p$ and 3$p$ lines of the yellow Rydberg series. Spatially selective excitation excludes substrate background and direct scatter, and the enhanced linear polarization of the grating-collected signal identifies the TE-like guided mode as the collection channel. These results establish the complete material--device--measurement stack for a novel platform of nonlinear quantum nanophotonics based on Rydberg excitons.

papers.title: Multi-Illumination Spectral Reflectance Reconstruction: A method for hyperspectral imaging using digital photography
papers.abstract: Quantitative measurement of complex coloration patterns is essential for many biological studies and practical applications. Although color perception depends on the observer's visual system, an objective characterization is possible by measuring the spectral reflectance across the sample surface. Traditional methods for measuring spectral reflectance are either limited in spatial resolution, as with spectrometer probes, or limited in spectral detail, as with digital cameras. We present a method for reconstructing spatially resolved spectral reflectance of samples from multiple images taken under different illuminants with known spectral irradiance. Using an optimization scheme that minimizes pixel-value error while regularizing for the smoothness of the reflectance spectrum, our method generates high-resolution hyperspectral images. We tested our method using both existing spectral reflectance datasets and original multi-illumination images taken in a custom photo-box, demonstrating high accuracy and simple implementation of the method, as well as the ability to infer how samples are perceived by different visual systems. Our method can be a useful tool for objective quantification of complex visual patterns in color-related biological research and imaging applications.

papers.title: Material optimization of optical properties of particulate products by transition matrix method and sequential global programming
papers.abstract: Material optimization of nanoparticle assemblies, such as structurally coloured photonic crystals, attracts increasing interest. We combine the transition matrix method (TMM), which avoids spatial discretization of particles and surrounding medium, with sequential global programming (SGP) to optimize optical properties of particulate products by iteratively assigning predefined catalogue materials to individual particles. We derive exact separable models, reproducing the fully coupled objective under single-particle material changes, and computationally accessible first-order correct approximations for general continuously differentiable objectives. These approximations aim to capture the nonlinear, potentially nonconvex dependence on individual material variables beyond their local first-order behaviour. Within SGP, globally minimizing the particle-wise subproblems can yield substantial improvements in few outer iterations, including steps away from unfavourable stationary points, as previously demonstrated for discrete dipole approximation-based SGP. The construction exploits the decomposition of the TMM system matrix into a material-dependent block-diagonal and a material-independent coupling matrix, while the state and adjoint problems remain fully coupled. Applications include extinction, scattering quantities, and colour objectives. In a 35-particle extinction minimization problem, the objective decreases by 31.0% in 13 iterations. A fine-grid evaluation of the fully coupled objective shows that no tested single-particle material change improves the final design. For a 627-particle photonic crystal, chroma increases by 58.4-122.1% for different particle diameters in 17-42 iterations. The optimized designs favour absorbing material in layers away from the incident light, consistent with experimental findings.

papers.title: Dephasing-free plasma acceleration with millijoule picosecond lasers
papers.abstract: Laser-plasma accelerators reach gradients a thousand times above radio-frequency cavities, but need joule-class femtosecond lasers firing about once per second, and electrons outrun the wave. A comb of laser lines spaced by the plasma frequency, each in its own mode of a matched channel, drives a wake moving at the speed of light. In particle-in-cell simulations a 175\,mJ, 0.5\,ps drive holds 21\,GV/m over 10\,mm with a 0.15\,rad phase drift; a test electron gains 208\,MeV, 2.6 times more than in one mode. Because the wave builds up resonantly, the required energy falls steeply with density: a 29\,mJ drive sustains 20\,GV/m, and a 10\,mJ drive, within reach of kilohertz industrial lasers, gives a test electron 170\,MeV over 30\,mm. A simulated stage transfers 5\,\% of the laser energy to the wake; the Manley--Rowe limit is about 18\,\% for five lines.

papers.title: Finite-Key Analysis for Multiple-Antenna Quantum Key Distribution with Continuous Variables
papers.abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) techniques, known for their use in wireless communications, can also find applications in quantum communications systems. This is, for instance, relevant to satellite-based quantum communications when atmospheric turbulence and the time-varying nature of the channel can make their implementation difficult. Here, we study the application of MIMO techniques to continuous-variable (CV) quantum key distribution (QKD) in the realistic setting where a finite number of signals are exchanged. We show how data collected during the brief overpass time of low-earth-orbit satellites over ground stations can be processed to estimate MIMO channel parameters, extract a secret key, and quantify the key generation rate. For $2\times 2$ MIMO settings with Gaussian encoding and heterodyne detection, our finite-key analysis indicates that MIMO CV-QKD could outperform both multiplexed (with a nominal 3~dB improvement) and single-mode (with a nominal 6~dB nominal improvement) scenarios. Furthermore, we conjecture that the ultimate enhancement of a multiple-antenna CV-QKD system can be characterized by the product of the number of its inputs and outputs.

papers.title: Efficient calculation of the full Laguerre-Gaussian spectrum of entangled biphotons
papers.abstract: The spatial biphoton state generated by spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) enables applications in high-dimensional quantum information processing and is often described in Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) modes. However, calculating the full LG spectrum for arbitrary radial and orbital angular momentum (OAM) indices requires computationally demanding multidimensional integrations. We present a generating-function approach that analytically performs the four-dimensional transverse spatial integral without approximating the phase-matching function. The source geometry can be completely described by a few dimensionless parameters, which reduce to two parameters for wave-vector-degenerate photons with equal waists. Our derived expressions for the full LG spectrum allow for computationally efficient and numerically stable evaluation at high mode orders, addressing a crucial obstacle in previous works. To illustrate our approach, we compare OAM spectra obtained by projection onto the lowest radial order and by radially insensitive detection, and investigate how high-dimensional maximal entanglement can be approached by tuning source parameters. Our results provide a new analytical tool for efficiently characterizing and engineering high-dimensional spatial entanglement in SPDC.
